I found out about this earlier today. I can't believe that a company is even attempting to do this... I would think that the "doge" image/name belongs to the public domain.

Thankfully -- as the article points out -- there's probably enough prior art that the existing dogecoin community could make a very strong case against any sort of trademark of "doge", since the origin of the term "doge" is more or less unknown.

The image, on the other hand, is trickier, at least of the original shiba inu image macro, since we know the origin of the image. Many of the other elements of "doge" branding, however (various dogecoin logos, for example) are probably safe due to prior art.
